content: Repaglinide is a medication prescribed to manage type 2 diabetes, a condition where the body does not use insulin effectively, leading to an inability to regulate blood sugar levels. This drug works by stimulating the pancreas to release insulin, which helps lower blood glucose levels. It may also be prescribed for other purposes; consult your doctor or pharmacist for additional information. Repaglinide is available in tablet form and is taken orally. It should be taken before meals, ideally within 30 minutes prior to eating or immediately before the meal. If you skip a meal, you must also skip the corresponding dose of repaglinide. Conversely, if you consume an additional meal, you should take an extra dose. Your doctor may adjust your dosage gradually based on your response to the medication. It is essential to follow the instructions on your prescription label carefully and consult your doctor or pharmacist if you have any questions. Take the medication exactly as prescribed, without altering the dose or frequency. Continue taking repaglinide even if you feel well, and do not discontinue it without consulting your doctor. Before starting repaglinide, inform your doctor and pharmacist if you are allergic to this medication or any other drugs. Additionally, disclose if you have a history of liver or kidney disease or if you have type 1 diabetes. Notify your doctor if you are pregnant, planning to become pregnant, or breastfeeding. If you become pregnant while taking repaglinide, contact your doctor immediately. If you are scheduled for surgery, including dental procedures, inform your healthcare provider that you are taking this medication. Follow all dietary and exercise recommendations provided by your doctor or dietitian. Maintain a healthy diet and discuss alcohol consumption with your doctor, as alcohol can lower blood sugar levels. If you miss a dose of repaglinide and have just started eating a meal, take the missed dose as soon as you remember. However, if you have already finished eating, skip the missed dose and resume your regular dosing schedule. Do not take a double dose to compensate for a missed one. Repaglinide may cause fluctuations in blood sugar levels. Be aware of the symptoms of both low blood sugar (hypoglycemia) and high blood sugar (hyperglycemia), and know how to respond to these conditions. Symptoms of hypoglycemia include shakiness, dizziness, sweating, irritability, mood changes, headache, numbness or tingling around the mouth, weakness, pale skin, hunger, and clumsy or jerky movements. Severe hypoglycemia can lead to confusion, seizures, or loss of consciousness, requiring immediate medical attention. Symptoms of hyperglycemia include extreme thirst, frequent urination, extreme hunger, weakness, and blurred vision. Untreated hyperglycemia can progress to diabetic ketoacidosis, a life-threatening condition characterized by dry mouth, nausea, vomiting, shortness of breath, fruity-smelling breath, and decreased consciousness. Contact your doctor immediately if you experience symptoms of hyperglycemia or diabetic ketoacidosis. Other potential side effects of repaglinide include headache, nasal congestion, joint pain, back pain, constipation, and diarrhea. Inform your doctor if these symptoms are severe or persistent. Store repaglinide in its original container, tightly sealed, and out of reach of children. Keep it at room temperature, away from excessive heat and moisture, and do not store it in the bathroom. Dispose of expired or unused medication properly, and consult your pharmacist for guidance on disposal. In case of an overdose, contact your local poison control center at 1-800-222-1222. If the individual has collapsed or is not breathing, call emergency services at 911. Attend all scheduled appointments with your doctor and laboratory to monitor your blood sugar levels and glycosylated hemoglobin (HbA1c). Your doctor will also instruct you on how to monitor your blood or urine sugar levels at home. Do not share your medication with others, and consult your pharmacist if you have questions about refilling your prescription. Repaglinide is sold under the brand name Prandin®.
